_description: Structural constants: values that shape the observation and action spaces, the module-ID naming contract, and the paths the visualizers read. These are real inputs - every module named by a _source key reads them through gym_continuousDoubleAuction/config_loader.py and holds no literal of its own. Per-run knobs live in train_config.json; env fallbacks live in env_defaults.json.
_note: Derived quantities are not listed. book_dim is book_rows * k_rows, snapshot_dim is book_dim + extra_dim, and the action space's price cardinality is k_rows. Writing a derived value here would create a second copy that can disagree with the first.

observation_layout._note: One observation snapshot is book_rows stacked rows of k_rows price levels - [bid_price, bid_size, ask_price, ask_size, bid_occupied, ask_occupied] - followed by extra_dim market-level scalars [log_mid, log1p_spread_ticks, mid_return, signed_volume, log1p_trade_count, trade_direction] - EXTRA_FIELDS in state_helper.py is the definition, and its length is checked against extra_dim at construction. The two occupancy rows (doc/15 S3-14) are 1.0 where a level holds an order and 0.0 where it does not, so a price entry of 0.0 is no longer ambiguous between an absent level and a resting quote sitting exactly at the reference price - measured at 1.2% of occupied cells under random play at the shipped config and 22% at a thin-book stress config before the rows existed. k_rows is the single definition of book depth: the observation exposes it, the action space's price code indexes it, and _set_price reshapes against it. book_rows is fixed by the six lists set_agg_LOB builds (BOOK_ROW_ORDER in state_helper.py); changing it requires changing that function.
observation_layout._note_private_dim: private_dim is the width of the PER-AGENT block appended after the n_hist stacked snapshots, so an observation is n_hist * snapshot_dim + private_dim floats. The book prefix is still shared and computed once; only this tail differs between agents. It exists because the reward is f(nav, prev_nav, max_nav, ...) and none of those were observable - two agents holding opposite positions saw the byte-identical vector and needed opposite actions, which no policy can do (finding S1-2). Changing this number means changing State_Helper.set_private_state to match; State_Helper.private_fields(k_rows) there is the single definition of what the block contains, and its length is checked against this value at construction. It is 9 base fields + 2 * k_rows own-book sizes + 2 own-order counts + 1 feedback flag: 9 + 20 + 2 + 1 = 32 at k_rows 10.
observation_layout._note_own_book: The OWN-BOOK block (doc/15 S3-24 phase 1, closing the S1-2 tail): for each of the k_rows public levels on each side, THIS agent's resting size at that level on the public book's sqrt(V / limit_max_size) scale (non-negative on both sides since S4-17), then this agent's resting order count per side over action_space.max_own_orders, then unmatched_last_step - 1.0 if the agent's last modify/cancel named no resting order (phase 3), so the consequence of a dead action is in the next observation. Level k of the own book is level k of the public book in the same snapshot, which is what lets a tokenising encoder carry own size as two extra channels of each level token (tokenize.py).

observation_bounds._note: Finite bounds of the observation Box (doc/15 S4-15), one [low, high] pair per feature family. State_Helper.observation_bounds builds the low/high arrays of the whole n_hist * snapshot_dim + private_dim vector from these, the env declares the Box with them, and set_next_state clips every emitted vector to them and counts the elements it clipped in num_obs_clipped_step (info, the episode record, and the obs_clip_fraction training metric). A bound is a claim about the range a feature can take, so the counter is what makes a wrong claim visible rather than a silent clip. The two occupancy rows are [0, 1] by definition. Every field named in BOOK_ROW_ORDER, EXTRA_FIELDS and private_fields() must have an entry here or in the own_size / own_count aliases; construction fails naming the field otherwise.
observation_bounds._note_derivation: Where a bound is a mathematical identity it is exact: with P > 0, bid_price (M - P) / M is < 1 and ask_price (P - M) / M is > -1; mid_return M_t / M_prev - 1 is > -1; position is a tanh; trade_direction, time_left, the counts and the flag are defined on [-1, 1] or [0, 1]; drawdown is <= 0; vwap_vs_mid is (M - VWAP) / M < 1; sizes, spread, trade count, cash_on_hold and the own-book block are >= 0. The other sides are measured (doc/16 section 16.22: 20 seeded episodes x 400 steps of random play at the shipped config and 20 at a stress config - 6 agents, 20,000 cash, anchors 5..500, tick 0.1) and given at least 4x headroom over the widest value seen. The price rows are signed on their measured side because every frame in the stack is normalised by the NEWEST frame's midpoint (doc/05 section 2.2): an older frame's bid resting above M_t reads negative. The first smoke test of a [0, 1] bid_price bound clipped 192 elements in 50 steps for exactly that reason. The wide price and cost-basis tails come from the price level itself random-walking down toward the tick floor under random play (doc/16 section 16.23: every extreme cell sat in a TWO-SIDED book whose midpoint had fallen to a few ticks, e.g. M = 2.5 with tick 1), where one tick is a large fraction of price and a level a dozen ticks away reads as a multiple of the midpoint - the coordinate problem of doc/15 S3-15, not the one-sided fallback. Their true extremes are set by the config, not by chance - log_mid's floor is log(min_tick) - log_mid_centre (-6.21 at the stress config, exactly the value measured), and ask_price, bid_price, mid_return and vwap_vs_mid can in principle reach (price / min_tick - 1). These bounds cover everything measured with headroom; a run whose book collapses further is counted, not hidden, in num_obs_clipped_step. For the log features the headroom is on the argument (e^8 = 2,981 trades per step against 9 seen; e^10 = 22,026 ticks of spread against 44 seen). The NAV-normalised ratios share one envelope of 8, i.e. eight times the starting NAV.

action_space._note: category_n is checked against the side/type mapping in _set_action_mkt_depth at construction, so a value that disagrees with that mapping raises instead of silently doing nothing. price_offset_n must be odd: the neutral 'join' code is the middle one, and offsets run from -(n//2) to +(n//2) ticks. The price code's cardinality is not here - it is observation_layout.k_rows.
action_space._note_order_slot: order_slot aims a modify or cancel at one of the agent's OWN resting orders on the named side, counted from the touch (best price first, oldest first within a level) - slot 1 is the order nearest the market - and clamped to the deepest own order when the agent has fewer than the slot names. For cancel, slot 0 means every own order on that side. For modify, slot 0 keeps the pre-slot FIFO rule (the oldest order) so a policy that ignores the head loses nothing; slot k moves the k-th order to the price named by price + price_offset. The only miss left, counted in num_unmatched_step, is a modify or cancel with nothing resting on that side. Cancel no longer matches by price at all; limit still does, as the upsert rule. max_own_orders is the cardinality minus one, set to the p90 of resting orders measured under random play (4; doc/16 16.19). Why clamp rather than miss: a head whose upper slots were dead made modify WORSE for a uniformly random policy - the baseline opponents - than the FIFO rule it replaced (48% -> 23% of issued modifies hit) while cancel only rose from 7% to 19%; a learned policy gains nothing from dead slots because it can read its own-order counts and aim exactly. Clamped, any slot hits whenever the agent has an order on that side (doc/16 16.20).

price_anchor_fallbacks._note: Two fallbacks for the price anchor, both normally overwritten by reset(). action_helper_last_price seeds self.last_price before the first reset; state_helper_midpoint is used when the book has no two-sided market and last_price is unusable. They are read from one place now, so they cannot drift apart.

module_id_prefixes._note: A naming contract, not a knob: SelfPlayCallback parses these prefixes to tell baseline opponents from champion snapshots. Changing them invalidates existing checkpoints, whose module directories are named with the old prefix.

runtime_env_vars._note: Set with setdefault before ray.init, so an existing value in the environment wins. Add entries here rather than in code.

logging._note: How the package configures the standard library logging module, applied once per process by the first get_logger call. level is the fallback: $CDA_LOG_LEVEL wins over it, which is how the level reaches Ray's worker processes - they are separate interpreters that never run train.main, so train.py exports the variable and each worker's first import picks it up. env_var is named here so the exporter and the reader agree on one string. The format carries the pid because with num_env_runners > 0 every worker logs into the same stream, and without it the episode hooks are unattributable. It also carries iter=, the training iteration, so a log line can be joined to the progress.jsonl row for the same iteration; it reads '-' in any process that does not know the iteration, which is every env runner. datefmt carries the date because a training run outlasts a day and a time-only stamp cannot be ordered across midnight.
logging._file_note: The run log. Until this existed the package logged only to stdout, so the narrative a run is diagnosed from - the per-episode NAV tables, the league statistics, the ERROR that precedes a strict_nav_check raise - survived only in scrollback, while progress.jsonl kept the numbers. file_name is written under log_base_dir, beside progress.jsonl. Rotation bounds it: file_max_bytes per file, file_backup_count old files kept, so a long or resumed run cannot fill the disk. Set file_name to an empty string to disable file logging entirely.
logging._file_worker_note: Every process writes its own file rather than sharing one, because RotatingFileHandler is not safe across processes - two of them crossing the size threshold together rename and truncate the same file underneath each other. The driver writes file_name; a worker writes the same name with its pid before the suffix (run.log -> run.4231.log). This matters rather than being a detail: the episode callbacks run on the env runners, so with num_env_runners > 0 the NAV tables and the conservation ERROR are emitted there and nowhere else. dir_env_var carries log_base_dir to those workers the same way env_var carries the level - they are separate interpreters that never run train.main.

visualize_paths._note: Default arguments of the visualize entry points. The per-step record is Parquet, written by train.episode_record.EpisodeRecorder under <episode_parquet_dir>/<run_id>/ (train_config.json's episode_data_dir). episode_parquet_fallback is the path tried when episode_parquet_dir does not exist, which is what happens when the visualizer is run from inside visualize/. The visualizer picks the most recently modified run_id directory unless one is passed explicitly. training_log_dir/training_log_fallback are the same pattern for progress.jsonl, one per-iteration JSON line written under <training_log_dir>/<run_id>/ (train_config.json's log_base_dir).
